scope: Pickup Observation, magnetic transduction, passive pickup/electronics, cable/load interaction; no product-tone adoption.

sources.title: Pickguard Assembly Stratocaster Wiring Diagram — SSS
sources.specimen_scope: Specific Fender SSS prewired pickguard assembly; topology evidence only unless a value is explicitly tied to this specimen.
facts: Three single-coil pickups are wired through a selector/control network to an output jack.
The documented assembly includes a 5-way switch, volume/tone controls, output jack wiring and grounding.

sources.title: Fender Modern Player Stratocaster HSS Wiring
sources.specimen_scope: Specific Fender Modern Player Stratocaster HSS model; component values/topology must not be universalized to all Strat-style guitars.
facts: The documented HSS instrument uses neck and middle pickups plus a two-coil bridge pickup.
The diagram includes a 5-way switch, volume/tone controls, output jack and a push/pull switching element.

sources.title: Acoustics and Modeling of Pickups
sources.publication: Journal of the Audio Engineering Society 60(10), 768-782 (2012)
facts: Pickup position and finite sensitivity width are modeled as distinct contributors to pickup timbre.
The modeled causal chain includes sensed string position, magnetic-flux mapping, time differentiation to induced voltage, and resonant filtering by the pickup electrical circuit.
An equivalent pickup circuit with inductance, winding resistance, capacitance and magnetic/core-loss representation is a useful candidate model.
Series and parallel pickup combinations alter the equivalent electrical network as well as signal magnitude/phase.
boundaries: The equivalent circuit is evidence for a candidate model class, not proof that a single low-order RLC representation is sufficient for every pickup and every transient.

sources.title: Cable Matters: Instrument Cables Affect the Frequency Response of Electric Guitars
facts: A passive magnetic-pickup guitar and its cable form an interacting resonant electrical system rather than a buffered source followed by an acoustically irrelevant cable.
Cable capacitance changed the measured/simulated frequency response in the studied systems.
In the measured cable set, inductance and series/parallel resistance effects were much smaller than capacitance effects.
The largest reported resonant-frequency shift among the measured cables was about 1.4 kHz.
boundaries: The relative insignificance of cable R/L is specific to the studied cables and conditions; it must not be promoted to a universal rule without validation.

sources.title: Interwinding Distributed Capacitance and Guitar Pickup Transient Response
sources.author: Peter Robert Kotiuga
facts: Distributed interwinding capacitance motivates higher-order pickup models when transient behavior is part of the target.
A simple lumped RLC model may be insufficient for reproducing all audible transient features.
boundaries: This is counter-evidence against prematurely declaring a low-order RLC model final; it does not prove that a distributed model is required for the project's eventual perceptual/realtime target.

SOURCE_FACT: Fender publishes distinct SSS and HSS Strat-style wiring topologies with selector, controls and output-jack boundaries.
Peer-reviewed pickup modeling literature treats pickup position/sensitivity width, magnetic transduction and the electrical resonant network as separable causal mechanisms.
Peer-reviewed cable research demonstrates that cable capacitance can materially shift the loaded response of passive magnetic-pickup guitar systems.
Peer-reviewed higher-order pickup research provides a credible counter-hypothesis to a universally sufficient low-order lumped RLC model.
MEASURED: The 2011 AES cable study reported up to approximately 1.4 kHz resonant-frequency shift across its measured cable set.
INFERRED: The project should preserve a position-dependent string observation boundary before magnetic transduction.
The Guitar Electrical Port must retain source-network information sufficient to reproduce cable/load interaction; a rendered WAV alone is not a sufficient electrical contract.
A low-order pickup equivalent circuit is an appropriate baseline candidate, but model order must be selected by falsification against frequency, phase and transient evidence.
HYPOTHESIS: For the intended Strat-style SSS/HSS use cases, a low-order pickup network plus explicit cable/load interaction may be sufficient over a declared operating domain if transient and loaded-response error stay below predeclared thresholds.
Finite pickup aperture and observation position may explain bridge/middle/neck spectral differences without post-EQ presets.
A reduced GuitarAmpElectricalLink may match a higher-accuracy network solver closely enough for realtime use.
next_measurement_requirements: pickup-position harmonic-structure comparison under identical excitation
pickup/network impedance or transfer response over frequency
transient error comparison between low-order and higher-order pickup candidates
